**Title:** Adaptive Ensembling: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Political Document Analysis

**Abstract:**
Insightful findings in political science often require researchers to analyze documents of a certain subject or type, yet these documents are usually contained in large corpora that do not distinguish between pertinent and non-pertinent documents. In contrast, we can find documents that relate to the specific topic of research through labels or information about its content. If we use all the documents in the large corpus, even those that are not relevant, the results of the model may not be accurate. But if we only use the documents that we know are relevant, we may be missing information that is useful. To find the solution, we propose a method called 'Adaptive Ensembling' that can select which documents are most useful from a large corpus. We tested it with some experiments that showed that it can work for political document analysis.

**Background:** In many cases of text classification in political science, the models of classification are trained with a lot of data and it is good data. But when the model is used for a new text that it has not seen before, it may not work well because the data was not like the new text. This is called a problem of 'domain adaptation'. We need a new model that can work in a new place with a new text even if the new text is not like the old text. We also need a model that can make the best use of the data, so that even the data that we are not sure if it is good or not can be used.

**Method:** We made a new method called 'Adaptive Ensembling'. It is a type of 'unsupervised domain adaptation' that can select which documents are most useful from a large corpus. It does this by finding the features of the documents that we know are most important, so that we can use all the other documents. We use a type of learning called'self-supervised learning'

Title: Effect of PT-Symmetric Operator on Coherence Under the Non-Markovian Environments

In this work, we mainly investigate the effect of PT-symmetric operation on the dynamic behavior of the relative entropy of coherence for a two-level system within non-Markovian environments and put forward a feasible physical scheme to recover coherence by using an optimal PT-symmetric operator. The non-Markovian environment, which is usually described by a memory kernel, will lead the coherence to decay with time in a non-exponential way. Here, we use PT-symmetric operator with a real parameter to modify the non-Markovian environment, the PT-symmetric operator can change the dissipipation of the system. We calculate the relative entropy of coherence for the system, the PT-symmetric operator can make the relative entropy of coherence bigger than without PT-s symmetric operation. We derive the expression of the PT-symmetric operator by use of the theory of linear matrix, we can get the optimal PT-s symmetric operator by find the maximum of the relative entropy of the system. By using the quantum mechanics theory and the method of numerical, we can get the result that the PT-syemt metric  operation can recovery the coherence for the system.

Here, our data demonstrate a critical role for the ubiquitin ligase complex, Sel1L-Hrd1, in the regulation of a key checkpoint in B cell development, which is essential for preventing the generation of auto-reactive or aberrant B cells. We utilized flow cytometric analysis and flow cytometric sorting to demonstrate that the loss of the Hrd1 component of the Se1L-Hrd1 complex results in an accumulation of immature pre-B cells and an increase in the death rate of B cell progenitors in mouse embryonic stem cells. This indicates that the loss of the Hrd1 component of the Se1L-Hr1 complex results in B cells that have defects in the assembly of heavy chain with light chain and this results in these B cells that have been made to die through apoptosis.

The assembly of heavy chain with light chain is critical for B cell development, because it is the selection mechanism that decides if a B cell will be a normal cell that can make antibodies or if it will be a bad cell that will make antibodies that are harmful to the body.
